extracted.intended_audience: owners/operators of CCR units, environmental compliance managers, site engineers, state/tribal permitting authorities, and environmental attorneys
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory requirements and performance standards for closing coal combustion residuals (CCR) units by removal, including timelines, certification, post-closure care, recordkeeping/website posting, and corrective action/groundwater remediation obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deadlines and time extensions for completion of closure
rubrics_metrics.description: The CCR regulations establish deadlines to initiate and complete closure activities (e.g., generally complete closure activities within five years for CCR surface impoundments and six months for CCR landfills). The regulations allow additional time provided the owner or operator can make prescribed demonstrations based on site-specific circumstances beyond the facility's control.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For impoundments 40 acres or smaller the maximum time extension is two years. For impoundments greater than 40 acres the maximum time extension is five 2-year extensions (10 years). For CCR landfills, maximum time extension is two one-year extensions (total two years). Owners/operators must substantiate factual circumstances demonstrating the need for each extension. The number of time extensions is capped. (§257.102(f))

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-closure care period and requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply existing post-closure care requirements at §257.104 to CCR management units (CCRMU) without revision; post-closure care criteria are essential to ensuring long-term safety.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Existing post-closure care requires monitoring and maintenance of units that have closed in place for at least 30 years after closure is completed. During post-closure, the facility must continue groundwater monitoring and corrective action where necessary. Revisions clarify the unit must be in detection monitoring to complete post-closure care. (§257.104)

rubrics_metrics.name: Recordkeeping, notification, and internet posting requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Owners/operators of CCRMU must comply with existing CCR recordkeeping, notification, and website reporting requirements in §§257.105 through 257.107, including establishing a public CCR website.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Owners/operators must record specific information in the facility's operating record, maintain files of demonstrations/plans/notifications/reports, notify State Director and Tribal authorities, and maintain a public CCR website titled 'CCR Rule Compliance Data and Information'. Information posted must be available at least five years from initial posting date unless specified otherwise. Posting must be completed no later than 30 days from submittal to the operating record. Owners/operators have 15 months from the effective date to establish the CCR website. Each file in the operating record must indicate the date it was placed and be retained for the retention period specified in §257.105. EPA provided a table in Unit III.D.5 detailing required records and retention periods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deferral to permitting for closures completed under other authorities
rubrics_metrics.description: Where units have closed under a State program, EPA may allow units to continue post-closure care under that State program or defer closure activities to permitting once criteria are met.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If criteria for deferral to permitting are met, the permitting authority (once authorized) can evaluate the site-specific closure and State post-closure activities and determine what further closure or post-closure activities are appropriate. This addresses units closed under regulatory authority and avoids duplicative requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Closure-by-removal performance standards (two standards)
rubrics_metrics.description: Closure by removal consists of two performance standards: (1) remove all CCR from the unit and decontaminate all areas affected by releases; (2) closure is complete when all CCR and areas affected have been removed and groundwater monitoring demonstrates no exceedances of GWPS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The second performance standard requires groundwater corrective action of a unit to be completed for closure to be considered complete. The revised regulatory text specifies closure by removal is complete when CCR has been removed; areas affected by releases have been removed or decontaminated; and groundwater monitoring concentrations of constituents in appendix IV do not exceed GWPS established pursuant to §257.95(h). (§257.102(c))

rubrics_metrics.name: Certification and notification of completed closure
rubrics_metrics.description: Owner/operator must obtain certification from a qualified professional engineer or approval from the Participating State Director (or EPA where EPA is permitting authority) verifying closure has been completed in accordance with the written closure plan and §257.102, and must prepare a notification stating closure is completed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The notification must be completed within 30 days of completion of unit closure and must include the required certification. Under prior structure, closure certification could not be completed until groundwater corrective action was completed; the final rule allows certain certifications where groundwater corrective action continues in post-closure only if other requirements (e.g., remedy implementation) are met. (§257.102(f)(3), §257.102(h))

rubrics_metrics.name: Deed notation requirement prior to post-closure care
rubrics_metrics.description: Prior to the start of the post-closure care period when using the closure-by-removal option, the owner/operator must record a notation on the deed that the land has been used as a CCR unit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This deed notation must be recorded before post-closure care begins and is one of the finalized requirements for using the closure-by-removal option. It supplements certification and notification requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Finalized requirements to use closure-by-removal option
rubrics_metrics.description: To close a CCR unit under the closure-by-removal option, the owner/operator must meet a set of requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requirements: (1) complete all removal and decontamination activities except groundwater during the active life of the unit; (2) with one exception, begin implementation of the corrective action remedy selected per §§257.96–257.97 during the active life (before completing closure); (3) complete groundwater corrective action during post-closure care; (4) amend written closure and post-closure plans to reflect this approach; (5) obtain certification or approval of closure completion within current time frames in §257.102(f); and (6) record the deed notation prior to post-closure. EPA revised §257.102(c) and §257.104(g),(h) accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of removal and decontamination activities
rubrics_metrics.description: Removal and decontamination activities include removing all CCR from the unit, CCR mixed with soils, CCR included in berms, liners, or other unit structures, and removing or decontaminating all areas affected by releases from the CCR unit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The final rule does not allow components of the unit constructed with CCR to remain in place if the unit is closing by removal. Although there are no soil cleanup numeric standards in the CCR regulations, if soil beneath the unit is contaminated sufficiently to serve as a secondary source of groundwater contamination, its removal may be required as part of source control in a remedy under §257.97. Contaminated groundwater must be remediated through the corrective action process (§§257.96–257.98).

rubrics_metrics.name: Implementation of selected remedy prior to certifying closure
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the closure-by-removal option, the owner/operator must have initiated remedial activities required by §257.98(a) prior to certifying that it has completed closure (to ensure impacted groundwater is returned to original conditions as soon as feasible).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Existing corrective action requirements remain unchanged: an assessment of corrective measures (ACM) must be initiated within 90 days of an SSL determination and completed within another 90 days (60-day extension possible). After ACM completion and public meeting, a remedy must be selected that meets prescribed standards (including attaining GWPS) and remedial activities must be initiated within 90 days of remedy selection. EPA explains that remedy implementation (including initial actions such as source control) is distinct from other closure activities and must commence within a reasonable schedule per §257.97(d) and §257.98.

rubrics_metrics.name: ACM and remedy selection timing and public participation
rubrics_metrics.description: An ACM (assessment of corrective measures) must be conducted and a public meeting held as part of the corrective action process prior to remedy selection; community input must be considered in remedy selection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ACM: initiate within 90 days of SSL, complete within 90 days (extension not to exceed 60 days). After ACM completion and public meeting, a remedy must be selected as soon as feasible and implementation scheduled per §257.97(d). EPA encourages public engagement elsewhere but will not require additional mandatory public meetings beyond those in the corrective action process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remedy performance standard: attainment of GWPS
rubrics_metrics.description: Selected remedy must meet prescribed standards including a requirement that the remedy attain the groundwater protection standards (GWPS).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Remedy selection must consider whether the remedy will attain GWPS established pursuant to §257.95(h). The corrective action program requires remedial activities to achieve GWPS and be pursued on a schedule to return groundwater to original conditions as feasible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independence of closure and corrective action obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: Closure requirements and corrective action requirements operate independently; facilities must comply with both and cannot delay corrective action while closure occurs, or vice versa.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Delaying remedy implementation until after closure would be inconsistent with §257.98(d) to complete remedial activities within a reasonable period. EPA rejects the concern that closure-by-removal would permit indefinite exceedances of GWPS or incentivize choosing the slowest, least protective remedies. Facilities remain subject to §§257.96–257.98 which prohibit such actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Constraints on selection of slow/least protective remedies (anti-pattern)
rubrics_metrics.description: Owners/operators may not exploit the closure-by-removal option to select remedies that unreasonably prolong groundwater exceedances (e.g., choosing natural attenuation solely to delay compliance).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The corrective action requirements and selection criteria (§257.97 and §257.98) limit unacceptable choices. The facility must have initiated remedial activities during the active life of the unit to be eligible for the closure-by-removal alternative, and documentation is required if corrective action was triggered near the end of closure and the facility could not extend active life.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitored Natural Attenuation (MNA) considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: MNA is a potential remedy but requires identification of attenuation mechanisms, characterization of site conditions, installation of monitoring wells, and ongoing performance monitoring; it does not necessarily require construction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA notes MNA can be implemented based on current and modeled conditions; installation of downgradient monitoring wells is a principal action. MNA would not meet §257.97(b) criteria if there is no evidence of viable permanent immobilization mechanisms under current or modeled conditions. Delaying monitoring/data collection (as would happen if remedy implementation were postponed) undermines MNA since data collection is critical.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to document and substantiate need for extensions and eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: To obtain additional time for closure, owners/operators must substantiate the factual circumstances demonstrating the need for the extension and document compliance with corrective action requirements if relying on the closure-by-removal option.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a facility triggered corrective action near the end of closure and could not extend the active life due to §257.102(f) deadlines, the facility must document: (1) compliance with §§257.96–257.98; and (2) that it could not extend the active life, consistent with §257.102(f). Facilities must provide factual support for claims that existing deadlines are infeasible to justify extensions beyond the regulatory caps.
